svg.title: Reach and safety collide at four points, so decide which side you want before each attempt
svg.desc: The upper half shows four pairs in tension, with what you want on the left and an arrow pointing to its cost on the right. Wanting ordinary people to believe you costs credibility, because credibility comes from a real name, a track record and existing relationships, which are exactly your exposure. Wanting to evade keyword filtering costs comprehension, because distorted wording only reads clearly to people who already agree, keeping you inside your own circle. Wanting the content to persuade costs safety, because persuasion rests on specific, checkable detail and specificity is what points back at you. Wanting to reach more people costs risk, because a wider spread moves closer to the thresholds written into the relevant provisions and makes you more likely to be treated as a priority case. The lower half gives three orientations: to leave a record, prioritise archiving the content outside the jurisdiction and keep the publisher's visibility as low as possible; to persuade specific people, work privately and at small scale and give up public reach; to spread the content, accept higher risk for the publisher, or hand the material to an existing channel willing to carry it.
svg.text: WHAT YOU WANT
WHAT IT COSTS
Ordinary people to believe you
An anonymous account carries little credibility. Credibility comes from a real name, a
track record and existing relationships, and those are exactly your exposure.
To evade keyword filtering
Distorted wording is hard to read. Only people who already agree decode it, which
keeps you inside your own circle.
Content that persuades
Persuasion rests on specific, checkable detail, and specificity is the part that points
back at you.
To reach more people
A wider spread moves closer to the thresholds written into the relevant provisions,
and makes you more likely to be treated as a priority case.
None of the four has a solution that gets both. Decide which side you want before each attempt.
To leave a record
Prioritise archiving the content
outside the jurisdiction.
Keep the publisher's visibility
as low as possible.
To persuade specific people
Work privately and at small scale.
Give up public reach.
To spread it
Accept higher risk for the publisher.
Or weigh handing the material to an
existing channel willing to carry it.
The risk does not land on you alone. Group administrators carry responsibility for what is posted, family and employers get contacted, and other members of
the same group can be affected.
Onward sharing is the part most often underestimated. Once content is reposted, screenshotted or reworked, the spread leaves your control while
responsibility can still return to the original source.
